weather.typical: Alpine North Cascades weather with rapid changes possible; expect cold nights and variable conditions even in midsummer given the remote, high-elevation setting
weather.probability: Afternoon thunderstorms and fast-moving weather systems are a real risk on the long, exposed ridge traverse in summer

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Loose rock and a long, committing approach are the primary consequence drivers; a fall or injury on the ridge is a serious problem given the remote position with no easy retreat

avalanche.zone: No NWAC zone directly forecasts this specific peak; nearest reference is the Washington Pass/SR-20 corridor zone, and NWAC generally does not issue forecasts during the July-September climbing window

seasonal_hazards.crevasses: Route reportedly skirts/crosses glacier ice near the Cosho-Kimtah col (the Kimtah/Mesahchie Glacier); minor crevasse hazard, greater when snow-covered early season, though this is not detailed in the on-file hazards list

_raw.seasonal_closures: Wilderness accessible mid-May through mid-October; Wilderness Information Center closed October 11 - May 14

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.notes: 60% of sites (Boston Basin/Eldorado/Sulphide Glacier/etc.) are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size limit is 12 in trail corridors and camps and in the Mount Shuksan, Eldorado Peak and Forbidden Peak cross-country zones, which this route is in; 6 in the remaining cross-country zones. Limits include people and stock. Boston Basin camping restricted to two designated sites (Low Camp ~5,300 ft, High Camp ~6,400 ft). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.seasonal: Cascade River Road (the access road for these trailheads) has a history of washouts/closures — check current NPS road-conditions page each season.
